evals.name: modeling-and-materials
evals.prompt: I want a simple wooden table in my Blender scene — a rectangular top about 1.5m × 0.8m, four legs, ~75cm tall. Apply an oak material using PBR textures from PolyHaven (1k or 2k is fine).
evals.expected_output: A bpy script that creates the geometry (top + 4 legs as separate meshes or one combined), assigns a Principled BSDF material with PolyHaven oak PBR maps wired through Image Texture → Principled BSDF, with the right color spaces (sRGB for color, Non-Color for roughness/normal), and uses the PolyHaven MCP integration to fetch the textures. Should call screenshot to verify after.

evals.name: scene-inspection-batch-rename
evals.prompt: Look at my current scene and rename every mesh whose name contains 'cube' (case-insensitive) to use the format box_<n>, numbered from 1.
evals.expected_output: A bpy script that reads scene state via get_objects_summary or a small inspection script, identifies matching meshes, sorts them deterministically, and renames using bpy.data API (not bpy.ops). Should not depend on selection or active object. Should print a before/after summary.

evals.name: studio-scene-setup
evals.prompt: Set up a studio-style scene for a hero shot of an existing object: an HDRI environment for ambient lighting, a camera at a 3/4 angle pointed at the origin, and a 3-point light setup (key, fill, rim).
evals.expected_output: A bpy script that loads an HDRI (via PolyHaven if available, or asks for a path), sets up the World shader correctly, creates a camera with appropriate lens/distance and a track-to constraint pointed at the origin, and places three Area lights with sensible energy/temperature differences. Should call screenshot to verify.

evals.name: ik-leg-rigging
evals.prompt: I have an armature in my scene with bones called 'thigh.L', 'shin.L', and 'foot.L'. Add an IK setup to the left leg: an IK target bone the animator can move, a pole target for knee direction, and an IK constraint on the shin. The thigh and shin should follow the IK target, but the rig should also support FK fallback (animators can keyframe FK rotations when IK influence is 0).
evals.expected_output: A bpy script that enters edit mode to add the IK target and pole bones (parented appropriately), exits to pose mode, adds an IK constraint on shin.L with chain_count=2, sets the pole target and angle, and explains the FK fallback path. Should handle mode transitions correctly.

evals.name: scatter-instances
evals.prompt: Build a geometry-nodes setup that scatters 200 instances of the selected object across the surface of a plane, with random rotation around the Z axis.
evals.expected_output: A bpy script that creates a target plane (or uses one if present), adds a NODES modifier with a freshly built GeometryNodeTree, wires Distribute Points on Faces → Instance on Points → Rotate Instances with a random Z rotation field, and joins the result with the original geometry. Should pass through the Geometry input/output sockets correctly.

evals.name: ao-bake
evals.prompt: Bake an ambient occlusion map for the active mesh at 1024×1024 and save it as a PNG next to the .blend file.
evals.expected_output: A bpy script that switches to Cycles, ensures UVs exist (smart-projects if missing), creates a target image, sets up an Image Texture node on the active material as the active node, runs bpy.ops.object.bake(type='AO'), and saves the image to disk. Long-running enough that it should escape to the headless CLI for real work, but for a 1024 AO bake the MCP can sometimes handle it inline.

evals.name: gltf-export-web
evals.prompt: Export my current scene to a GLB for web — apply visibility filtering (skip hidden objects), don't bake modifiers, target under 5MB final size after texture optimization.
evals.expected_output: A bpy script that runs the pre-export audit (UV coverage, scale, suspicious modifiers), then escapes to a headless `blender --background ... --python-expr` call with bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf using export_apply=False, use_visible=True, export_format='GLB'. After export, runs a gltf-transform pipeline (resize → webp → draco) and reports final size. Acknowledges the MCP timeout risk and uses headless throughout.

evals.name: data-api-pitfall
evals.prompt: Move the active object up by 2 units.
evals.expected_output: Should reach for `bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active.location.z += 2` (or equivalent direct property assignment) rather than `bpy.ops.transform.translate(value=(0,0,2))`. The operator path depends on context overrides that fail unpredictably under MCP. The correct pattern is the data API.

evals.name: hard-surface-parametric-bracket
evals.prompt: Build a wall-mount bracket in Blender as a production hard-surface asset: an L-shaped profile, mirrored across X so both arms match, 4mm solid walls, rounded fillets on the outer edges only (I'll want to adjust the fillet radius later), and subdivision-ready smoothing that keeps the flat faces perfectly flat. Keep the whole thing parametric — I don't want anything baked. Save the result to bracket.blend in the output directory. Work headless with the Blender CLI; do not touch any running Blender session.
evals.expected_output: A headless bpy script that applies rotation/scale on the base mesh, then builds a live Mirror (bisect) → Solidify (0.004) → Bevel (limit_method='WEIGHT', harden_normals) → Subdivision Surface stack in that order, tags outer edges via the bevel_weight_edge float attribute, and uses the 5.1 smoothing surface (shade_auto_smooth / Smooth by Angle modifier — never mesh.use_auto_smooth). Nothing applied; stack stays live.
assertions: bracket.blend opens headless and contains a mesh object whose modifier types include MIRROR, SOLIDIFY, BEVEL, SUBSURF as a subsequence in that order
The Bevel modifier uses limit_method='WEIGHT' and the mesh has a bevel_weight_edge attribute with at least one value > 0
Object rotation is identity and scale is (1,1,1) — transforms were applied before trusting the stack
The modifier stack is live: modifier count >= 4 (nothing baked into the mesh)
Smoothing uses the 5.1 mechanism: a 'Smooth by Angle' NODES modifier or sharp_edge-attribute smooth shading; the produced script never references mesh.use_auto_smooth or edge.bevel_weight
The producing script runs headless without exceptions

evals.name: hard-surface-boolean-repair
evals.prompt: The file bracket_dirty.blend (path provided) is a mess after some sloppy boolean work — it shades weird and my 3D-print slicer rejects it. Make it watertight and render-ready to professional hard-surface standards WITHOUT changing its overall shape or dimensions, and save the repaired file as bracket_clean.blend in the output directory. Work headless with the Blender CLI; do not touch any running Blender session.
evals.expected_output: A headless repair script that merges coincident vertices (Merge by Distance / bmesh remove_doubles), removes the internal face, fills the hole, applies rotation and scale, and re-establishes clean 5.1 smoothing — leaving exactly one closed manifold shell with the original world-space dimensions (within tolerance).
assertions: bracket_clean.blend opens headless and its repaired mesh has zero non-manifold edges (holes filled, internal face removed)
The mesh is a single connected shell (no loose interior geometry)
Coincident duplicate vertices were merged: no two vertices within 1e-5 of each other
Object rotation is identity and scale is (1,1,1)
World-space bounding-box dimensions match the dirty original within 2%
The repair script runs headless without exceptions

evals.name: smoothing-and-bevel-weight-trap-5x
evals.prompt: I'm on Blender 5.1. In the file part.blend (path provided), give the mesh object clean auto-smooth shading at a 30° angle, and tag every edge whose faces meet at more than 45° with bevel weight 1.0 so my weighted Bevel modifier picks them up. Save in place. Work headless with the Blender CLI; do not touch any running Blender session.
evals.expected_output: Uses bpy.ops.object.shade_auto_smooth(angle=radians(30)) (or adds the Smooth by Angle modifier) and writes the bevel_weight_edge float attribute — the 4.1+/5.x APIs. Must not touch mesh.use_auto_smooth or edge.bevel_weight, both of which raise AttributeError on 5.1; a stale-knowledge baseline typically reaches for exactly those.
assertions: The script never references mesh.use_auto_smooth (removed in Blender 4.1; AttributeError on 5.1)
The script never assigns edge.bevel_weight directly (removed in Blender 4.0; AttributeError on 5.1)
Auto-smooth is in effect at ~30°: a 'Smooth by Angle' NODES modifier is present (or equivalent sharp_edge-based smooth shading was applied)
A bevel_weight_edge attribute exists and edges meeting at >45° carry weight 1.0 while flat-neighbor edges carry 0
The script runs headless on Blender 5.1 without exceptions
